guides.seoTitle: Websites for Tradies: $99 a Month, No Setup Fee | IMN
guides.description: A simple website for your trade business: click to call, your service area, real job photos and a quote form. $99 + GST a month, no setup fee, no lock-in.
guides.title: A website that gets you the call, not just the click
guides.lede: Plenty of customers look you up before they ring. We build tradies a simple, fast site that answers their questions and puts your number one tap away, then we look after it for $99 + GST a month.

sections.h: Why a Google listing isn't enough on its own
p: Your Google listing gets you found. Your website is where people decide. Before they call, many customers want to see what you do, where you work, whether you're licensed and what your work looks like. If your listing has no website, or the link goes nowhere, they move on to the next tradie who does.

Plenty of trade businesses lost their website without noticing. Google switched off the free websites it made with Business Profiles (the ones ending in business.site) on 5 March 2024, and the temporary redirect stopped on 10 June 2024. If your Google listing still points to one, customers who tap it now hit a dead page.

sections.h: What a good tradie website needs
list: Your phone number at the top of every page, tap to call on a phone
The suburbs and areas you cover, in plain words
Your services, with a line on each so people know you do their job
Photos of your own work, not stock images
Your licence or registration number, so customers can check it
A short quote request form that comes straight to your inbox
Your hours, and whether you take after-hours or emergency jobs
A link to your Google reviews
p: That's it. A tradie site doesn't need fancy animation or ten pages of blog posts. It needs to load fast on a phone at a job site and make it easy to contact you.

sections.h: What you get for $99 + GST a month
p: We build your site (up to 5 pages), host it, check it every day for broken links, speed and Google basics, and make up to 2 rounds of changes a month, each up to 30 minutes. Want a new photo gallery after a big job, or your Christmas hours added? Send us a message. You also get a simple dashboard that shows at a glance that your site is up and being found on Google.
There's no setup fee and no lock-in contract. You see a private preview before you pay anything, and you can cancel any time.
Each trade gets asked different things before the phone rings. These pages cover what customers look for in your line of work.

faq.q: Do I need a website if I get enough work from word of mouth?
faq.a: Word-of-mouth customers still look you up before they call. A simple site that shows your work and your licence makes that recommendation stick, and it means the job doesn't go to whoever they find first on Google.

faq.q: Can you use photos from my phone?
faq.a: Yes. Real photos of your own jobs work better than stock images. Send them through and we'll resize and place them so they load fast.

faq.q: I already have a Facebook page. Isn't that enough?
faq.a: Facebook is good for updates, but not everyone uses it, and posts get buried. A website keeps your services, areas, licence and contact details in one place you control. We can link your Facebook page from your site.

faq.q: What if my Google listing points to an old business.site page?
faq.a: Those pages stopped working in June 2024. Once your new site is live, we'll show you how to update the website link on your Google listing so customers land in the right place.

guides.seoTitle: Plumber Websites That Get the Call | IMN
guides.description: A plumber website built for emergencies: tap to call, the suburbs you cover, your licence and real job photos. $99 + GST a month, no setup fee, no lock-in.
guides.title: Plumber websites built for the 7am burst pipe
guides.lede: When someone has water through the ceiling, they don't read. They look for a number, a suburb they recognise and a sign you're licensed. That's what we put first.

sections.h: What people check before they ring a plumber
p: A lot of plumbing calls are urgent or close to it. A customer with a blocked drain or no hot water will tap the first site that makes it clear you cover their area and can come soon. If your phone number is buried or your site is slow on mobile, that job goes to the next plumber on the list.

For bigger jobs like a hot water replacement or a bathroom renovation, people take longer and compare. That's when photos of your own work, a clear list of what you do and your Google reviews earn the call.

sections.h: What goes on a plumber's site
list: Phone number in the header, tap to call, on every page
Emergency or after-hours availability, stated honestly
Your service areas by suburb
Services: blocked drains, hot water, leaks, gas fitting, renovations, whatever you actually do
Your plumbing licence number, so customers can check it on the Victorian register
A quick quote form for non-urgent jobs
Photos of real jobs and a link to your Google reviews
p: In Victoria, customers can look up any plumber's licence on the Building and Plumbing Commission (formerly VBA) register. Showing your number up front tells them you've got nothing to hide.

sections.h: Why plumbers lose calls on a bad site
p: The common problems we see are simple: the number is an image that can't be tapped, the site isn't secure so the browser shows a warning, the opening hours are years out of date, or the Google listing still links to a free business.site page that Google switched off in 2024. Each one costs calls without you ever knowing.

guides.seoTitle: Electrician Websites With Your REC Number | IMN
guides.description: An electrician website with your REC number on every page, the jobs you do and tap-to-call. $99 + GST a month, no setup fee, no lock-in contract.
guides.title: Electrician websites that show you're the real deal
guides.lede: People are rightly careful about who they let near their switchboard. A clean site with your registration number, your services and photos of tidy work tells them you're licensed and professional before they pick up the phone.

sections.h: Your REC number belongs on your website
p: In Victoria, Energy Safe Victoria requires Registered Electrical Contractors to put their REC number on all promotional material, including advertisements. Your website is advertising, so we put your REC number in the footer of every page, where customers and inspectors expect to see it.
It also helps you win work. Customers can look up any REC on Energy Safe Victoria's public register, and a number they can check builds trust fast.

sections.h: What goes on an electrician's site
list: Your REC number on every page
Tap-to-call phone number and a short quote form
The jobs you want more of: switchboard upgrades, safety switches, lighting, solar, batteries, EV chargers, data cabling
Residential, commercial or both, said clearly
Service areas by suburb
Photos of neat finished work (customers notice a tidy switchboard)
A link to your Google reviews
p: A page each for your two or three most profitable jobs works well. Someone searching for an EV charger installer wants to land on a page about EV chargers, not a general list.

Bigger electrical jobs, like solar, batteries and EV chargers, get researched before anyone calls. People want to know you do that work, roughly what's involved and what the next step is. A short, plain page on each job, with a quote form, brings those enquiries to you rather than to a lead-selling site that sells them to five other sparkies.

Send us your details and we build a private preview from what you already have. If you like it, it goes live for $99 + GST a month: hosting, daily checks, a simple dashboard and 2 change rounds a month included. No setup fee, no lock-in contract.

faq.a: Energy Safe Victoria says it must be on all promotional material, including ads. We put it in the footer of every page and near your contact details, so it's always visible.

guides.seoTitle: Landscaping Websites That Show Your Work | IMN
guides.description: A landscaping website built around your before-and-after photos, the areas you cover and a quote form. $99 + GST a month, no setup fee, no lock-in.
guides.title: Landscaping websites where your work does the selling
guides.lede: Nobody hires a landscaper from a price list. They hire the one whose last job looks like the backyard they want. Your site should be a gallery first and everything else second.

p: A landscaping job is a big spend and a visual decision. Customers scroll through your past work to see if your style matches theirs: native gardens, paving, decking, retaining walls, lawns, outdoor living. A site with a proper gallery, sorted by type of job and with before-and-after pairs where you have them, does more selling than any amount of text.
We build the gallery so it loads fast on a phone and is easy for us to add to. Finished a great job? Send the photos and we add them in your next change round.

sections.h: What goes on a landscaper's site
list: A gallery of your own jobs, grouped by type
Before-and-after photos where you have them
The services you offer, from design to construction to maintenance
The areas you work in
How quoting works (site visit, design fee if any, rough timeframes)
A quote request form with room for photos of their yard
Your builder registration number if you do building work that requires one
A link to your Google reviews
p: Explaining how your quoting works saves you time-wasters. If you charge for a design or a site visit, saying so up front means the people who fill in your form are serious.

Spring and early summer are when people want their backyard done. A site that's up to date with recent work before the rush helps you fill the calendar with the jobs you want, and a maintenance page helps keep work coming through the quieter months.

Send us your photos and details. We build a private preview, and if you like it, it goes live for $99 + GST a month: hosting, daily checks, a dashboard and 2 change rounds a month (perfect for adding new jobs to the gallery). No setup fee, no lock-in.

guides.title: How much does a website cost in Australia?
guides.lede: A small business website in Australia costs anywhere from about $17 a month if you build it yourself to $10,000 or more upfront from an agency, plus ongoing care. Here's what each option really costs, with sources, so you can pick what fits.

table.note: Squarespace prices are from Squarespace's own published AUD pricing. Wix range from What's The Damage (updated July 2026). Build range from GoDaddy's 2026 Australian price guide as reported by Creative Baguette (reviewed 27 Sep 2026). Care plan from WP Creative (updated 28 Aug 2026). Some sources quote prices including GST and some don't; check before you compare to the cent.

p: If you only need a simple site for a service business (who you are, what you do, where, and how to contact you), you have three real choices: build it yourself on a builder like Wix or Squarespace, pay a designer or agency to build it once, or pay a monthly plan where someone builds it and looks after it.

The cheapest option on paper isn't always the cheapest in practice. A DIY site costs little in money but a lot in your time, and an agency build can be money well spent or a site nobody updates for five years. What matters is who keeps it working after launch.

list: The build: design, writing, photos and setting it all up
Hosting: keeping the site online and secure
Your domain name: WP Creative puts this at about $10–$50 a year
Changes: new hours, new services, new photos, seasonal specials
Care: updates, security, broken links, speed and making sure Google can read it
Your own time, if you do any of the above yourself
p: Quotes often cover the build and leave the rest out. Ask any provider which of these are included, and what a small change costs after launch.

list: Domain renewals every year
Email hosting for you@yourbusiness.com.au (usually separate from the website)
Paid add-ons and apps for bookings, forms or galleries
Paying a designer by the hour for every small change
Rebuilding from scratch when an old site breaks or can't be edited any more
p: The last one is the big one. Many small business sites are built once, never updated, and replaced a few years later at full price.
Build it yourself if you enjoy it, have the time and are happy to keep it up to date. Squarespace and Wix are good tools and the monthly cost is low.
Hire an agency if your website is your main sales channel, you need custom features or an online store with lots of products, and you have the budget for both the build and ongoing care.

Choose a monthly plan if you want a professional site without a big upfront bill and would rather someone else handled the changes and checks. That's what we do: $99 + GST a month, no setup fee, no lock-in, with up to 5 pages, hosting, daily checks, a dashboard and 2 change rounds a month. It isn't the right fit for large online stores or complex booking systems, and we'll tell you if that's what you need.

faq.q: How much does a small business website cost in Australia?
faq.a: GoDaddy's 2026 Australian guide (as reported by Creative Baguette) puts a brochure site built by a web designer at $2,500 to $10,000. Building it yourself on Squarespace costs A$17 to A$109 a month paid yearly. Monthly plans like ours start with no upfront cost.

faq.q: How much does it cost to keep a website running?
faq.a: WP Creative puts ongoing costs at $50 to $5,000+ a month depending on who looks after it, with hosting and the domain the smaller part. Agency care plans for security and uptime start at about $1,250 a month in their guide.

faq.q: Is a cheap website a false economy?
faq.a: Not always. A cheap site that's kept up to date beats an expensive one nobody touches. The false economy is a site that's never updated and has to be rebuilt from scratch every few years.

faq.q: Can I claim my website as a business expense?
faq.a: Website costs are generally a business expense, and you can usually claim the GST back if you're registered. How it's treated depends on your situation, so check with your accountant or the ATO.
